items.title: Conditions
items.body: Events occur independently, at a constant average rate \(\lambda\), and singly in time/space. \(X\sim\text{Po}(\lambda)\).

items.title: Mean and Variance
items.body: \(E(X)=\text{Var}(X)=\lambda\). The mean equals the variance — a key identifying feature.

items.title: Cumulative Tables
items.body: Use Poisson tables for \(P(X\leq r)\). Note \(P(X\geq r)=1-P(X\leq r-1)\). Additive: \(X+Y\sim\text{Po}(\lambda_1+\lambda_2)\).

items.title: Changing the Interval
items.body: If \(X\sim\text{Po}(\lambda)\) per hour, then in \(t\) hours: \(X\sim\text{Po}(\lambda t)\).

body.en: If events occur at a constant average rate \(\lambda\) independently, \(X\sim\text{Po}(\lambda)\) with: \(P(X=r)=\dfrac{e^{-\lambda}\lambda^r}{r!}\) for \(r=0,1,2,\ldots\)  ·  \(E(X)=\lambda\), \(\text{Var}(X)=\lambda\). Poisson approximation to Binomial: if \(n\) is large, \(p\) is small, \(np=\lambda\) is moderate (\(n>50, p<0.1\)), then \(B(n,p)\approx\text{Po}(\lambda)\).

Probabilistic Normalization & Moment Structure: Every probability model is governed by total probability conservation: \(\sum_x P(X=x) = 1\) for discrete random variables and \(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)\,dx = 1\) (with \(f(x) \ge 0\)) for continuous density functions. Expected value \(\mathbb{E}[X]\) acts as a linear operator (\(\mathbb{E}[aX + bY] = a\mathbb{E}[X] + b\mathbb{E}[Y]\)), whereas variance scales quadratically and adds for independent variables: \(\operatorname{Var}(aX \pm bY) = a^2\operatorname{Var}(X) + b^2\operatorname{Var}(Y)\).

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Poisson Distribution)

body.en:
Why Variance Scales as \(a^2\) and Independent Variances Always Add: By definition, \(\operatorname{Var}(Y) = \mathbb{E}[(Y - \mu_Y)^2]\). For \(Y = aX - bW\) with independent \(X, W\), subtracting its mean \(\mu_Y = a\mu_X - b\mu_W\) gives:

\[ \operatorname{Var}(aX - bW) = \mathbb{E}\!\left[(a(X - \mu_X) - b(W - \mu_W))^2\right] = a^2\mathbb{E}[(X-\mu_X)^2] - 2ab\,\operatorname{Cov}(X,W) + b^2\mathbb{E}[(W-\mu_W)^2] \]

Because independence implies \(\operatorname{Cov}(X, W) = 0\), the cross term vanishes and \((-b)^2 = +b^2\), proving \(\operatorname{Var}(aX - bW) = a^2\operatorname{Var}(X) + b^2\operatorname{Var}(W)\). Uncertainty compounds whether random variables are added or subtracted.

Faults in a wire occur at a rate of 2 per metre. Find the probability of (a) exactly 3 faults in 1 m, (b) fewer than 2 faults in 0.5 m.

(a) \(\lambda=2\): \(P(X=3)=\dfrac{e^{-2}\cdot8}{6}\approx0.1804\).

(b) \(\lambda=1\): \(P(X<2)=P(0)+P(1)=e^{-1}+e^{-1}=2e^{-1}\approx0.7358\).

\(X\sim B(200,0.02)\). Use a Poisson approximation to find \(P(X=5)\).

\(\lambda=200\times0.02=4\). \(P(X=5)=\dfrac{e^{-4}\cdot4^5}{120}=\dfrac{1024e^{-4}}{120}\approx0.1563\).

Problem (Medium): The box plot for dataset \( f \) has quartiles \( Q_1 = 20 \), median \( M = 30 \), and \( Q_3 = 41 \). Work out the interquartile range \( x = Q_3 - Q_1 \) of \( f \).

Step-by-Step Solution: The interquartile range is \( Q_3 - Q_1 = 41 - 20 = 21 \).

Problem (Hard): For finite sets \( A \) and \( B \), \( |A| = 71 \), \( |B| = 53 \), and \( |A \cap B| = 39 \). Work out the union cardinality \( x = |A \cup B| \).

Step-by-Step Solution: By Inclusion-Exclusion, \( |A \cup B| = 71 + 53 - 39 = 85 \).

rows.en: Produces smaller or even negative variance for the difference of independent variables.
Always add variances of independent variables: \(\sigma_{X-Y}^2 = \sigma_X^2 + \sigma_Y^2\).
Confuses the variance of the sample mean \(\sigma^2/n\) with its standard error.
Absence of sufficient evidence against \(H_0\) does not prove \(H_0\) is true.
Write in context: "There is insufficient evidence at the \(\alpha\) level to reject \(H_0\)."

body.en: Exam Marking Tip (Cambridge International A Level (9709 Paper 3 / Paper 6)): Always state the distribution parameters explicitly (e.g., \(X \sim \operatorname{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)\) or \(\bar{X} \sim \operatorname{N}(\mu, \sigma^2/n)\)) and sketch a quick shaded bell curve before standardizing to \(z = \dfrac{x - \mu}{\sigma}\). This secures the method mark even if a rounding slip occurs later.

label.en: ⚠️ Cambridge 9709 Traps — Linear Combinations vs Scaled Multiples in Poisson

body.en:
Sum of Independent Poisson Variables: If \(X_1 \sim \text{Po}(\lambda_1)\) and \(X_2 \sim \text{Po}(\lambda_2)\) are independent, then their sum is Poisson: \(X_1 + X_2 \sim \text{Po}(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2)\).

Scalar Multiples Are NOT Poisson: In contrast, \(2X_1\) is NOT a Poisson random variable because it can only take even integer values (0, 2, 4, ...). Its variance is \(\text{Var}(2X_1) = 4\text{Var}(X_1) = 4\lambda_1 \neq E(2X_1) = 2\lambda_1\). Always distinguish between observing two separate intervals (use \(X_1 + X_2\)) versus doubling the count of one interval (use \(2X_1\)).

question.en: The number of accidents on a highway follows a Poisson distribution with mean 1.6 per week. (a) Find the probability of at least 3 accidents in a 2-week period. (b) Given that at least one accident occurs in a week, find the probability that there are exactly 2 accidents in that week.

solution.en:
(a) In a 2-week period, the parameter scales to \(\lambda = 1.6 \times 2 = 3.2\):

\[P(X \ge 3) = 1 - P(X \le 2) = 1 - e^{-3.2}\left(1 + 3.2 + \frac{3.2^2}{2}\right) = 1 - 9.32e^{-3.2} \approx 1 - 0.3799 = 0.620\text{ (3 s.f.)}\]

(b) For 1 week, \(\lambda = 1.6\). Use conditional probability:

\[P(X = 2 \mid X \ge 1) = \frac{P(X = 2)}{P(X \ge 1)} = \frac{\frac{e^{-1.6}(1.6)^2}{2}}{1 - e^{-1.6}} = \frac{1.28e^{-1.6}}{1 - e^{-1.6}} \approx \frac{0.2584}{0.7981} \approx 0.324\text{ (3 s.f.)}\]

question.en: [Practice 4 · Medium] A cumulative frequency distribution \( f(x) \) has \( Q_1 = 29 \), median \( 41 \), and \( Q_3 = 55 \). Work out the spread \( \text{IQR}(f) = Q_3 - Q_1 \).

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Poisson Distribution and start from \( f(x) \).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \( Q_3 - Q_1 = 55 - 29 = 26 \).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

solution.en: From the cumulative frequency curve, \( Q_3 - Q_1 = 55 - 29 = 26 \).
